findings.title: Invoke the commit callback on the consumer thread
findings.body: This invokes the Commit callback supplied by StreamProcessor from commit_thread, concurrently with consumer polling, partition callbacks, and shutdown. Arroyo's processor and consumer offset bookkeeping are not synchronized for this concurrent use, so committing can race changes to partition assignments or consumer closure. Exceptions are only logged here rather than surfaced to the processor. Workers should record completions, while poll/join publish those offsets on the processor thread.

findings.title: Do not reuse a queue pool after its strategy shuts it down
findings.body: The factory constructs one queue_pool and passes it to every strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down. Arroyo recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so the strategy created after the first rebalance receives stopped workers and shutdown queues. Queue submission then raises ShutDown, which submit catches and marks complete, allowing valid results to be committed without processing. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy lifecycle, or implement safe reuse.

findings.title: Bound the queues and implement backpressure
findings.body: queue.Queue() has no capacity limit, and submit always accepts messages without checking backlog. If processing is slower than Kafka consumption—or one worker stalls—the consumer continues retaining decoded results, original payloads, and tracked offsets indefinitely. Unlike the existing bounded batch processing, this can exhaust memory instead of leaving the backlog in Kafka. Use bounded queues and nonblocking MessageRejected handling when capacity is exhausted.

findings.title: Do not mark failed processing as completed
findings.body: An exception escaping result_processor is logged, but the finally block still completes that item's offset. The commit loop can therefore advance past a result that was never successfully processed, permanently skipping it on restart. The exception handler in submit similarly completes messages that failed to be queued. Preserve or surface these failures rather than treating them as successful completion. The new error-handling test checks before the one-second commit interval, so it does not detect this behavior.

findings.title: Drain accepted work and flush offsets before closing
findings.body: close stops the commit thread before workers finish, and pool.shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before queued work is drained. Consequently, accepted messages remain unprocessed and work completed during shutdown has no final commit. Workers exceeding the fixed five-second join can also continue after close/join returns, racing a replacement partition owner. Implement close/join so accepted work drains within the requested timeout, completion offsets are flushed, and workers cannot outlive a successful join.

findings.title: Control worker execution before asserting a nonempty queue
findings.body: The workers run immediately and the test processor only appends to a list. They can process all ten submissions before get_stats executes, making total_items zero even when the pool works correctly. This introduces a scheduling-dependent test failure. Hold workers on an event until the queue-depth assertions finish, then release them and verify completion.
